objective: Reach [MONEY_1] and [NUMBER_1] teams in [NUMBER_2] months without raising a seed round.
brief: [COMPANY_1] is building [OTHER_1], an automated workflow auditing engine for mid-size operations teams in [OTHER_2] and [OTHER_3]. Founder [PERSON_1] left [COMPANY_2] to launch the product. Current ARR is [MONEY_2] across [NUMBER_3] design partners including [COMPANY_3], with [PERCENT_1] monthly growth. We plan to launch a self-serve tier at [MONEY_3] per seat on [DATE_1] to reach [NUMBER_1] teams without raising a seed round from [OTHER_4].

rounds.userMove: Launch as described in the brief with a [NUMBER_4]-day self-serve trial at [MONEY_3] per seat.

generalMoves.headline: Enterprise buyers extend procurement cycles past trial windows as budgets tighten.
generalMoves.move: We decline to convert the trial into paid seats at [DATE_1], citing internal policy reviews and the need for security compliance sign-offs that require three months of deliberation. Mid-size operations teams are freezing discretionary software spend and renewing existing contracts rather than onboarding unproven vendors without dedicated implementation support.
generalMoves.rationale: This exploits the assumption that self-serve trials convert smoothly without enterprise-grade procurement and security friction, starving the business of the cash needed to reach [MONEY_1].
generalMoves.targets: Mid-size operations teams will rapidly convert from a self-serve trial to paid seats.

generalMoves.headline: Bundling basic workflow auditing into our enterprise tier at no cost.
generalMoves.move: We are routing a team of eight engineers to package the core auditing features requested by [COMPANY_3]'s profile into a standard module for our existing customers. Since our roadmap is locked for months on custom enterprise requests, offering this as a complimentary bundle to our broad base costs us nothing in near-term development flow. We will match the self-serve pricing point with a zero-cost tier for our base, neutralizing the willingness to pay for [COMPANY_1].
generalMoves.rationale: This exploits the player's lack of capital and runway by giving away the exact functionality they are trying to monetize before they can scale their self-serve funnel.
generalMoves.targets: Mid-size operations teams will pay [MONEY_3] per seat instead of taking a free bundled alternative.

generalMoves.headline: Skeptical VC passes on seed terms and calls portfolio allies.
generalMoves.move: I will decline to issue a term sheet at your requested valuation, noting that market comps have softened significantly this year. Instead, I am quietly advising our existing enterprise portfolio company in the adjacent workflow automation space to accelerate its own mid-market auditing features. Let us see how easily you scale past [NUMBER_1] teams when a better-funded incumbent blocks the door.
generalMoves.rationale: This exploits the vulnerability of trying to scale organically into a market where well-capitalized adjacent players can easily add your feature set before you reach critical mass.
generalMoves.targets: Can self-serve motion scale to [NUMBER_1] teams without heavy capital burn or defensive moats?

rounds.userMove: Convert all [NUMBER_3] design partners including [COMPANY_3] to annual pre-paid contracts with a [PERCENT_2] discount and ship cross-vendor connectors that [COMPANY_2] cannot bundle.

generalMoves.headline: Mid-market buyers lock in annual renewals with existing vendors, ignoring new connectors.
generalMoves.move: We accept the annual renewal terms offered by our current supplier, locking in our workflow budget for the next twelve months. We choose not to deploy the new cross-vendor connectors from [COMPANY_1] because our internal teams have no capacity to migrate operational workflows mid-year without a dedicated implementation manager. The [PERCENT_2] discount fails to trigger movement because our discretionary software budget for this fiscal year is already fully allocated.
generalMoves.rationale: Locking design partners into annual deals secures cash flow, but it fails to crack the wider mid-market where procurement freezes and locked-in incumbent contracts prevent adoption of [OTHER_1].
generalMoves.targets: Mid-size operations teams will abandon existing annual contracts to adopt new workflow connectors.

generalMoves.headline: Skeptical VC asks portfolio company to match cross-vendor connectors.
generalMoves.move: I appreciate the hustle in locking in your design partners on annual prepays, but it does not solve your distribution problem or your lack of capital. I am instructing our portfolio company in the adjacent space to prioritize building those exact same cross-vendor connectors within the quarter. Without a seed round to fund your customer acquisition, you will bleed cash trying to out-build an entrenched incumbent.
generalMoves.rationale: This exploits the assumption that a bootstrapped team can out-engineer and out-market a well-funded incumbent once they enter each other's feature territory.
generalMoves.targets: Bootstrapped engineering velocity can outpace a well-funded incumbent's feature replication.

generalMoves.headline: We release native cross-vendor connectors and lock in multi-year enterprise agreements.
generalMoves.move: We appreciate [PERSON_1] securing those design partners, but we are deploying our engineering resources to release a native suite of cross-vendor connectors ahead of schedule. Simultaneously, our account management team is offering our existing enterprise base an extended multi-year package that incorporates these integrations at no additional charge. This effectively neutralizes the moat [COMPANY_1] is trying to build with proprietary interoperability.
generalMoves.rationale: By matching their new integration feature and absorbing it into our existing enterprise contracts, we remove the unique value proposition of [OTHER_1] before they can scale it. We are exploiting their lack of a locked distribution base by locking ours down tighter.
generalMoves.targets: Cross-vendor connectors can protect [COMPANY_1] from being commoditized by our free bundle.

rounds.userMove: Drop paid search completely; distribute free SOC2 workflow templates through compliance communities in [OTHER_3] and [OTHER_2] to keep payback under [NUMBER_5] days.

generalMoves.headline: Compliance communities ignore unverified templates as security audits shift to incumbent vendors.
generalMoves.move: We download the free SOC2 templates from [COMPANY_1] for internal policy reference, but we route our actual compliance audit through our incumbent security software provider rather than adopting an unproven auditing engine. Our risk committee requires vendor-backed indemnification for any workflow automation touching regulated data, which a community template distributed for free cannot provide. We allocate our engineering hours toward our existing vendor's integrated compliance modules instead of installing independent scripts.
generalMoves.rationale: Free templates bypass budget friction but fail to clear enterprise risk and procurement hurdles without dedicated vendor support and indemnification.
generalMoves.targets: Compliance community distribution eliminates acquisition cost and friction to achieve rapid self-serve adoption.

generalMoves.headline: Releasing free certified compliance templates natively integrated into our enterprise dashboard
generalMoves.move: We see [COMPANY_1] pivoting toward community-driven distribution of compliance templates, so we are having our team package pre-vetted SOC2 workflow templates directly inside our platform at no extra charge. We will share these certified frameworks across the exact same compliance communities in [OTHER_3] and [OTHER_2] to intercept [PERSON_1]'s top-of-funnel traffic before they reach the self-serve tier. It is a pleasure to let smaller players do the heavy lifting of community education while we capture the intent.
generalMoves.rationale: By distributing identical templates for free inside an established enterprise ecosystem, we remove the incentive for mid-size teams to adopt an unproven tool just for documentation.
generalMoves.targets: Free compliance templates driving organic acquisition without paid search.

generalMoves.headline: Skeptical VC flags community-led growth limits and passes on funding.
generalMoves.move: I appreciate the creative pivot to organic distribution through compliance communities, but relying entirely on zero-cost viral loops to hit [MONEY_1] without capital is wishful thinking. I am officially passing on this round, and I have already briefed our partners that we will not back any direct overlap with our existing portfolio footprint. Good luck bootstrapping against a well-funded incumbent holding the enterprise keys.
generalMoves.rationale: This move exploits the fatal flaw in the boot-strapped timeline by proving that organic community loops cannot generate sufficient enterprise pipeline velocity to replace a venture-backed sales force.
generalMoves.targets: Organic compliance community distribution can scale revenue to [MONEY_1] without paid acquisition or capital.
